edition.locus: Gebhardt XIII.I (preface; Marianus and James named)

source_text: Quotiens aliquid beatissimi martyres dei omnipotentis et Christi eius festinantes ad promissa regna caelorum carissimis suis uerecundius mandant, memores humilitatis quae semper in fide solet facere maiores, quanto modestius petiuerunt, tanto efficacius impetrauerunt. Et nobis quoque hoc praedicandae gloriae suae munus dei testes nobilissimi reliquerunt, Marianum dico, ex dilectissimis fratribus nostris, et Iacobum, quos mihi scitis praeter communem sacramenti religionem, uitae etiam societate et domesticis affectibus inhaesisse. Qui contra saeuientis saeculi pressuras et gentiles impetus habituri tam sublime certamen, praelium suum, quod instinctu spiritus caelestis inierunt, in notitiam fraternitatis per nos uenire iusserunt, non quod in terris uellent coronae suae gloriam per iactantiam praedicari, sed ut praecedentibus experimentis multitudo plebis et dei populus ad exemplum fidei posset armari. Nec inmerito id obsecuturo mihi fiducia familiaris iniunxit. Quis enim dubitet quae nobis in pace uitae communitas fuerit, quando nos indiuidua dilectione uiuentes unum tempus persecutionis inuenerit?
pass_a_gloss: As often as the most blessed martyrs of almighty God and his Christ, hurrying to the promised kingdoms of the heavens, entrust anything with modest reserve to their dearest friends, mindful of the humility which in faith is accustomed always to make greater, by how much more modestly they asked, by so much more effectually they obtained. And to us also this duty of proclaiming their glory the most noble witnesses of God have left behind, I mean Marianus, from among our most beloved brothers, and James, whom you know clung to me beyond the common bond of the sacrament also by sharing of life and by household affection. They, about to have so lofty a contest against the pressures of a raging age and the attacks of the heathen, ordered that their battle, which they entered at the impulse of the heavenly Spirit, should come to the knowledge of the brotherhood through us, not because they wished the glory of their crown to be proclaimed on earth through boasting, but so that by preceding proofs the multitude of the plebs and the people of God might be armed toward an example of faith. Nor undeservedly has familiar trust laid this upon me as one who will obey. For who would doubt what community of life was ours in peace, when one time of persecution found us living in undivided love?
pass_b_english: Whenever the most blessed martyrs of almighty God and of his Christ, hastening toward the promised kingdom of heaven, lay some charge upon their dearest friends with a becoming modesty, remembering the humility that in faith always makes men greater, the more modestly they asked, the more powerfully they prevailed. To me also, in the same way, those most noble witnesses of God have left this office of declaring their glory, I mean Marianus, one of our dearest brothers, and James, who, as you know, were bound to me not only by our common share in the sacrament but also by fellowship of life and by close household affection.

As they were about to face so sublime a conflict against the crushing force of a raging world and the assaults of the pagans, they commanded that their battle, undertaken at the prompting of the heavenly Spirit, should be made known to the brotherhood by my means, not because they desired to have the glory of their crown heralded on earth out of vainglory, but so that, through trials gone before, the multitude of the congregation and the people of God might be armed for the pattern of faith. Nor without good cause has intimate friendship imposed this duty upon me, ready to obey. For who could doubt what our common life was in time of peace, seeing that one season of persecution found us living together in undivided love.

lemmas.gloss: most blessed, here honorific for martyrs

choices.why: comparative adverb modifies the act of entrusting and pairs with memores humilitatis and quanto modestius, so it marks humble restraint rather than secrecy

choices.english: the task of proclaiming their glory
choices.why: munus with gerundive is a duty laid on the author, not a gift received, and praedicandae governs gloriae as its object
rejected: the gift of their glorious preaching

choices.term: in notitiam fraternitatis per nos uenire
choices.english: to reach the knowledge of the brotherhood through us
choices.why: in notitiam uenire is motion into awareness and per nos names the author as intermediary, not the martyrs coming themselves
rejected: to come to visit the brotherhood
